# **Introduction**

Duration: 3:00

Moving from simple stateless chatbots to production AI agents requires persistent cross-session memory, live external tool integration, and rich interactive interfaces. Building these capabilities manually across cloud infrastructure, APIs, and frontend frameworks can take days.

In this hands-on lab you will build, test, and deploy a **Restaurant Discovery Agent** powered by **Gemini 4 Neon** using the [Agent Development Kit (ADK)](https://adk.dev/), [Vertex AI Agent Runtime](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/overview) (Sessions and Memory Bank), [Google Maps Platform](https://developers.google.com/maps), and [A2UI (Agent-to-UI)](https://adk.dev/integrations/a2ui/). You will perform most of the work with natural language prompts in the [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli).

## **What you'll build**

You will build a multi-tool ADK agent that remembers a user's dining preferences across sessions, combines Google Search grounding with live Google Maps Places lookups, runs on a managed remote Agent Runtime backend, and renders three interactive A2UI surfaces inside the ADK Web UI: a dining preferences form, a clickable Google Maps location and radius picker, and a side-by-side results explorer.

* **Agent Development Kit (ADK)** is an open-source framework for building, testing, and deploying multi-tool AI agents in Python.  
* **Vertex AI Agent Runtime (Sessions and Memory Bank)** provides managed remote session storage (VertexAiSessionService) and cross-session long-term memory (VertexAiMemoryBankService) with managed and custom memory topics.  
* **Google Maps Platform** supplies live restaurant discovery, geocoding, and interactive maps via the Places API (New), Geocoding API, and Maps JavaScript API.  
* **A2UI (Agent-to-UI)** lets agents return declarative UI definitions—such as forms, interactive maps, and split-pane explorers—that render natively inside the ADK Web UI.

## **What you'll learn**

* How to set up and launch the Antigravity CLI with lab skills in Cloud Shell.  
* How to provision a service-restricted Google Maps Platform API key.  
* How to create an Agent Runtime backend for remote Sessions and Memory Bank with custom memory topics.  
* How to create, locally test, and deploy a Gemini 4 Neon ADK agent that combines Google Search grounding and the Google Maps Places API.  
* How to verify remote sessions in the Playground and inspect saved memories in Memory Bank.  
* How to enhance your agent with interactive A2UI components for collecting preferences, picking a starting point and search radius on Google Maps, and exploring results side by side.

## **What you'll need**

* A Google account. A personal Gmail account is required if you want to claim Google Developer Program credits.  
* A Google Cloud project with billing enabled. The next steps show how to claim credits and create a project.  
* A web browser such as Chrome.  
* Basic familiarity with the command line. No prior ADK or A2UI experience is needed.

# **Claim Google Developer Program credits**

Duration: 3:00

Enable\_GDP\_Credits\_Banner: True

If you are doing this lab along with an instructor, follow the instructions provided by the instructor or ask the instructor if these steps should be followed. If you are doing this lab on your own, follow the steps below.

All Google Cloud projects need an active Cloud Billing account. You can run this lab with free Google Developer Program credits. Claiming the credits creates a new billing account with the credits added, and you then create a new project that uses that billing account. If you already have a billing account, go directly to the **Create a new project** section of this step. If you already have a project with billing enabled, skip to the next step.

### **Claim the credits**

1\. Make sure that you are signed in to your personal Gmail account. If you are not, sign in first.

2\. On the credits banner at the top of this step, click **Activate**. If prompted, complete the form to set up your **Google Developer Program profile**.

3\. A QR code appears. Scan it with your phone and complete the reCAPTCHA check to verify that you are not a bot.

4\. Click **View Billing**. It can take a couple of minutes for the new billing account to appear.

### **Create a new project with the new billing account**

1\. Open [https\://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate](https://console.cloud.google.com/projectcreate) to create a new project.

2\. If a **Billing account** field is shown, select the billing account that was just created. The field is shown only if you have more than one billing account. Then click **Create**.

3\. Click the project selector next to the **Google Cloud** logo at the top left of the screen.

4\. Select the project that you just created. Your new project now uses the new billing account.

# **Project setup**

Duration: 5:00

1\. Go to the [Google Cloud console](https://console.cloud.google.com).

2\. Select your project in the project selector at the top left of the Google Cloud console. This is the project that you created in the previous step, or an existing project that has billing enabled.

3\. In this lab you will use the [Cloud Shell Editor](https://docs.cloud.google.com/shell/docs/launching-cloud-shell-editor) to perform all tasks. Open the [Cloud Shell Editor](https://ide.cloud.google.com/).

4\. On the sidebar of the Cloud Shell Editor, click **Open Folder**. If you do not see **Open Folder**, click the **File** icon on the left-hand side of the menu.

5\. Your home folder should already be selected. Click **OK** so your home folder becomes the root folder for this lab.

6\. Open the terminal, if it is not already open, by clicking **Terminal \> New Terminal** from the menu. You run the commands in this lab in the Cloud Shell terminal.

7\. Check that you are authenticated by running the following command in the Cloud Shell terminal.

&nbsp;

| gcloud auth list |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

8\. If you cannot remember your project ID, list all your project IDs.

&nbsp;

| gcloud projects list |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

9\. Copy the project ID and set it as the active project.

&nbsp;

| gcloud config set project \<YOUR\_PROJECT\_ID\> |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

10\. Confirm your active project.

&nbsp;

| gcloud config list project |
| :---- |

# **Enable APIs**

Duration: 2:00

Enable the core Google Cloud APIs needed for Vertex AI Agent Runtime and container deployment. Run the following command in Cloud Shell. It can take a minute to finish.

&nbsp;

| gcloud services enable \\     aiplatform.googleapis.com \\     cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com \\     apikeys.googleapis.com \\     cloudbuild.googleapis.com \\     artifactregistry.googleapis.com |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

## **Introducing the APIs**

* **Vertex AI / Agent Platform API** (aiplatform.googleapis.com) provides Gemini models and Vertex AI Agent Runtime (Sessions and Memory Bank).  
* **Cloud Resource Manager API** (cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com) lets tools and SDKs read project metadata to verify project identity and permissions.  
* **API Keys API** (apikeys.googleapis.com) lets you create and restrict Google Maps Platform API keys.  
* **Cloud Build API** (cloudbuild.googleapis.com) and **Artifact Registry API** (artifactregistry.googleapis.com) build and store the container image when deploying your agent to Agent Runtime.

# **Set up the Antigravity CLI**

Duration: 5:00

The [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli) (agy) is an AI coding agent that runs in your terminal and is pre-installed in Cloud Shell. In this lab you will use it to provision cloud resources, create and deploy your ADK agent, and build A2UI components using prompts.

## **Install the Agents CLI and lab skills**

The [Agents CLI](https://google.github.io/agents-cli/guide/getting-started/) (agents-cli) helps coding assistants such as the Antigravity CLI create, test, and deploy agents built with the [Agent Development Kit (ADK)](https://adk.dev/).

Run the following commands in the Cloud Shell terminal to create the project folder, install ADK and the Agents CLI, and install the lab skills.

&nbsp;

| \# Install uv if you do not have it installed yet pip install uv  \# Create the project folder and a Python virtual environment mkdir \~/advancedagents cd \~/advancedagents && uv venv source .venv/bin/activate  \# Install ADK and set up the Agents CLI uv pip install google-adk uvx google-agents-cli setup  \# Install the Antigravity skills for this lab npx skills add \<SKILLS\_REPO\_URL\> \--agent antigravity \-g |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

| Note: If you ever need to restart the terminal, go back to the project folder and activate the Python environment again with cd \~/advancedagents && source .venv/bin/activate. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

## **Launch the Antigravity CLI**

1\. Set the environment variables so that the Antigravity CLI signs in with Application Default Credentials (ADC) and uses your project's quota, then launch the CLI.

&nbsp;

| export AGY\_ADC\_AUTH=true export CLOUDSDK\_CORE\_PROJECT=\$(gcloud config get project) export GOOGLE\_CLOUD\_QUOTA\_PROJECT=\$(gcloud config get project) agy |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

| Note: If the terminal area is too small, the setup screens may not be fully displayed. Enlarge the terminal panel before you continue. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

2\. On first launch, select a theme with the arrow keys and press **Enter**.

3\. Accept the terms of service.

4\. When prompted to trust the folder, select **Yes, I trust this folder** and press **Enter**.

5\. Confirm that the Antigravity CLI is running in your project and pointing to the **advancedagents** folder.

&nbsp;

| Tips: The setup screens can differ slightly between Antigravity CLI versions. Press Shift+Tab to auto-approve file edits so that you only confirm commands. Run /model to change the model. If you leave the CLI with /quit, run agy \--resume to continue your previous session. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

# **Provision a Google Maps Platform API key**

Duration: 3:00

Your agent uses the Google Maps Platform to geocode locations, look up restaurants via the Places API (New), and render interactive maps in A2UI. In this step you ask the Antigravity CLI to enable the required Maps APIs and create a restricted API key.

&nbsp;

| Note: The output of an LLM can vary, so what the Antigravity CLI does in your environment may differ slightly from this lab. Use the steps as a guideline, and approve the commands that the CLI asks to run by pressing Enter. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

1\. Enter the following prompt in the Antigravity CLI.

&nbsp;

| We need to use Google Maps API in this codelab, so if the API key for Google Maps API key is not present, create it. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

2\. Approve the commands that the CLI asks to run. Behind the scenes, the Antigravity CLI enables the Google Maps Platform services (Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), and Geocoding API), creates a service-restricted API key, saves GOOGLE\_MAPS\_API\_KEY to .env, and adds .env to .gitignore.

# **Create an Agent Runtime backend for sessions and memory**

Duration: 5:00

Instead of storing conversation history in a local database, you will provision a managed [Vertex AI Agent Runtime](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/overview) (ReasoningEngine) resource. A single Agent Runtime backend provides both **Sessions** (VertexAiSessionService) for multi-turn conversation state and **Memory Bank** (VertexAiMemoryBankService) for cross-session long-term memory.

## **Provision the Session and Memory Bank backend**

1\. Enter the following prompt in the Antigravity CLI.

&nbsp;

| In Agent Runtime Create a new backend to hold Session and Memory that our agent can use. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

The Antigravity CLI provisions an Agent Runtime backend (advancedagents-session-memory-backend in us-central1) configured with four built-in managed memory topics (USER\_PERSONAL\_INFO, USER\_PREFERENCES, KEY\_CONVERSATION\_DETAILS, and EXPLICIT\_INSTRUCTIONS), and saves SESSION\_SERVICE\_URI and MEMORY\_SERVICE\_URI to .env.

## **Add custom Memory Bank topics**

To capture structured dining preferences alongside the built-in managed topics, add four custom memory topics.

1\. Enter the following prompt in the Antigravity CLI.

&nbsp;

| Add the following topics to the Long term memory: Preferred food type Allergies Preferred price range Name |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

Each topic is configured as a CustomMemoryTopic with a label and description that tells Memory Bank what dining facts to extract and consolidate across sessions, then applied to your live Agent Runtime backend.

# **Create and test the ADK agent**

Duration: 10:00

In this step you create a **Restaurant Discovery Agent** powered by **Gemini 4 Neon** that combines Google Search grounding with live Google Maps Places lookups and uses your remote Agent Runtime backend for sessions and memory.

## **Create the agent**

1\. Enter the following prompt in the Antigravity CLI.

&nbsp;

| Create an ADK Agent that can take user input like "Find me restaurants near shibuya", then do google search and look at google maps and find the restaurants near shibuya. Use remote session previously created and memory bank created in previous steps. Use gemini 4 Neon as the main model for the agents. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

Behind the scenes, the Antigravity CLI scaffolds the ADK project and wires up:

* **Google Search grounding and Places API:** Combines Google Search with a live Google Maps Places API (New) lookup tool returning verified names, addresses, ratings, review counts, price levels, and Google Maps links.  
* **Gemini 4 Neon:** Configured as the main model on the Vertex AI global endpoint while sessions and memory continue routing to us-central1.  
* **Remote Sessions and Memory Bank:** Configured to connect adk web and deployed endpoints to your remote Agent Runtime SESSION\_SERVICE\_URI and MEMORY\_SERVICE\_URI rather than local storage.

## **Test the agent locally**

1\. Open a second terminal (**Terminal \> New Terminal**), leaving the Antigravity CLI running in the first terminal.

2\. Navigate to the project folder, activate the virtual environment, and launch the ADK Web UI.

&nbsp;

| cd \~/advancedagents source .venv/bin/activate adk web \--allow\_origins "\*" |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

![][image1]

*Figure 1: Press Ctrl+Click on http\://127.0.0.1:8000 to open the ADK Web UI*

3\. Open **http\://127.0.0.1:8000** (or use Cloud Shell Web Preview on port 8000) and test the agent with a request such as I am looking for restaurants around shibuya area.

![][image2]

*Figure 2: Testing the Restaurant Finder agent in the ADK Web UI*

4\. When you finish testing, return to the second terminal and press **Ctrl+C** to shut down the ADK server.

# **Deploy to Agent Runtime and verify remote sessions**

Duration: 10:00

Next, deploy your containerized ADK agent directly to your Vertex AI Agent Runtime resource so it runs as a managed service sharing the same remote sessions and Memory Bank.

## **Deploy the agent**

1\. Switch back to the first terminal where the Antigravity CLI is running and enter the following prompt. Building and deploying the container image can take several minutes.

&nbsp;

| Deploy the agent to agent runtime. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

The Antigravity CLI runs agents-cli deploy, packages the project with your .env settings, and deploys the agent onto your advancedagents-session-memory-backend Agent Runtime instance.

## **Verify remote sessions in the console**

1\. Open the [Agent Platform Sessions](https://console.cloud.google.com/agent-platform/sessions) page in the Google Cloud console and find your session ID.

2\. Click the three-dot menu on the right-hand side of the session row and select **Open in Playground**.

![][image3]

*Figure 3: Opening a remote session in the Playground from the Sessions page*

3\. Inspect the session events and conversation history in the Playground to verify that your session is stored remotely.

![][image4]

*Figure 4: Inspecting remote session content in the Playground*

# **Add an A2UI dining preferences form**

Duration: 8:00

[A2UI (Agent-to-UI)](https://adk.dev/integrations/a2ui/) lets ADK agents return declarative UI definitions that render as interactive cards, inputs, and buttons inside the chat. In this step you add a web form card that collects the user's four Memory Bank topics on initial use and saves them directly to Memory Bank.

## **Add the preferences form component**

1\. In the Antigravity CLI terminal, enter the following prompt.

&nbsp;

| Add a component to ask for all the user information to be included in the memory, It should look a bit like a web form, this is in A2UI. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

2\. Start the local ADK server again in your second terminal (adk web \--allow\_origins "\*") and open **http\://127.0.0.1:8000**.

3\. Start a conversation (for example, hi). On initial use, the agent renders the **Dining Preferences & Memory Profile** form. Enter your **Name**, **Preferred Food Type**, **Allergies / Dietary Restrictions**, and **Preferred Price Range**, then click **Save Preferences to Memory**. Once saved, the form does not reappear on future sessions and your preferences are applied silently in the background.

![][image5]

*Figure 5: Dining Preferences & Memory Profile form rendered with A2UI*

## **Verify saved memories in Memory Bank**

1\. Open [Memory Bank](https://console.cloud.google.com/agent-platform/memory-bank) in the Google Cloud console and select your Agent Runtime backend.

2\. Click **Service configuration** (the gear icon) and open the **Memory bank** tab to confirm your managed and custom topics.

![][image6]

*Figure 6: Opening Service configuration from your Agent Runtime backend*

![][image7]

*Figure 7: Configured Memory Bank managed and custom topics*

3\. Switch to the **Memories** tab to confirm that your four dining preferences have been saved.

![][image8]

*Figure 8: Saved user dining preferences in Memory Bank*

# **Add interactive Google Maps A2UI components**

Duration: 10:00

Instead of asking clarifying questions in plain text or printing long markdown lists of restaurants, you will add two interactive Google Maps A2UI surfaces: a location and radius picker when a search begins, and a side-by-side results explorer when results return.

## **Add the location and radius picker**

1\. In the Antigravity CLI terminal, enter the following prompt.

&nbsp;

| When the user begins search for restaurants, A2UI should come with a UI that has approximate location that user has asked that can be edited and within how many kms. It should also show this in google maps and user should be able to click on any location and that will be start point. There should be a dropdown that sets how many kms from the starting point should be searched for the restaurants in users budget and users preferences. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

2\. Restart adk web \--allow\_origins "\*" (or hard-refresh the browser), click **\+ New Session**, and enter I am looking for restaurants around Shibuya area.

3\. The agent geocodes your approximate location and displays an interactive Google Map with a shaded radius circle. Click any point on the map to move the starting pin (or edit the address field), choose a distance from the **Search Radius (km)** dropdown (0.5 km to 10 km), and click **Search Restaurants Within Radius**.

![][image9]

*Figure 9: Interactive Google Maps starting point and search radius picker in A2UI*

## **Add the side-by-side results explorer**

1\. In the Antigravity CLI terminal, enter the following prompt.

&nbsp;

| Once the search is executed, show the search results in google maps in A2UI along with restaurant list and number of stars on the side of the map and once you click the pin drops or the name of the restaurant in the list, the details about that particular restaurant should be visible in A2UI interface, next to google maps. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

2\. Re-run your search in the ADK Web UI. The agent renders a split-pane results explorer: numbered restaurant pin drops on the Google Map on the left, a scrollable restaurant list with star ratings on the right, and a live details panel next to the map that updates whenever you click a pin drop or a restaurant name.

**![][image10]**

*Figure 10: Side-by-side Google Maps results explorer with restaurant list and details panel*

## **Redeploy the updated agent (optional)**

To push the final A2UI-enabled agent container to Vertex AI Agent Runtime, run the deployment prompt again in the Antigravity CLI.

&nbsp;

| Deploy the agent to agent runtime. |
| :---- |

# **Clean up**

Duration: 3:00

To avoid ongoing charges, delete the resources that you created in this lab.

## **Option 1: Clean up with the Antigravity CLI**

Ask the Antigravity CLI to remove the resources that it created.

&nbsp;

| Delete the Agent Runtime backend advancedagents-session-memory-backend in us-central1 and the Google Maps API key "Advanced Agents Codelab Maps Key" that you created in this project. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

Review each command before you approve it. Then exit the CLI with /quit.

## **Option 2: Clean up manually**

1\. Delete the advancedagents-session-memory-backend instance in [Vertex AI Agent Engine](https://console.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/agents/agent-engines).

2\. Delete the Advanced Agents Codelab Maps Key API key in [APIs & Services \> Credentials](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials).

3\. Delete the project folder in Cloud Shell.

&nbsp;

| cd \~ rm \-rf \~/advancedagents |
| :---- |

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

| Note: If you created a project only for this lab, you can instead delete the whole project to remove everything at once. |
| :---- |

&nbsp;
